Mumbai Student Launches Grassroots Initiative to Connect Domestic Workers with Welfare Benefits

01 Nov 2026, 11:22 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: timesofindia.indiatimes.com

Image: The Times of India · Source image rights not independently verified · Photo source · Cropped to 16:9 for the website

Addressing a Financial Disparity

A 17-year-old student from Mumbai, Ayaan Wadhwa, has launched an initiative called 'Workers of India' aimed at helping domestic workers navigate the complex landscape of government welfare schemes. The project was inspired by a personal experience in his own household, where a long-term employee requested a loan due to a family medical emergency, revealing a lack of basic financial safety nets and insurance.

Bridging the Information Gap

Wadhwa discovered that while many domestic workers are eligible for government support, such as the e-Shram portal, they often lack the awareness or technical assistance required to register. His approach to solving this includes:

  • Simplified Literature: Creating booklets in Hindi and Marathi to explain complex government policies.
  • On-Site Workshops: Partnering with residential housing societies to hold in-person registration camps.
  • Digital Support: Assisting workers in navigating government portals directly on-site to ensure successful enrollment.

To date, these workshops have facilitated the registration of over 750 workers across Mumbai for various welfare schemes. The effort has received acknowledgment through the International Baccalaureate Global Youth Action Fund in 2026.

Future Plans and Technological Scaling

Moving beyond manual registrations, Wadhwa is developing an AI-powered WhatsApp chatbot intended to assist workers in generating bilingual employment contracts. By allowing users to provide employment terms via voice messages in Hindi, Marathi, or English, the tool aims to simplify the documentation process for those unfamiliar with complex digital forms.

Verifying Information

Readers interested in the details of the 'Workers of India' initiative can look for updates via the project's official channels or inquiries through local residential committees in Mumbai that host similar outreach camps. The government's e-Shram portal remains the primary digital resource for workers seeking to register for social security and welfare benefits nationally.
